column1: # Labeled cases for scripts/jev-triage.sh --replay, built from confirmed drift in closed target-audit issues and scripts/target-audit/signals.tsv.
# Each claim is what agnostic-ai said before the fix; each excerpt is a short quote of the vendor text that settled it.
# The says_nothing rows pair a claim with vendor text from the same target that does not address it.

column3: claim
column4: excerpt

column3: agnostic-ai writes OpenHands MCP servers to the project `config.toml` under a `[mcp]` table with `sse_servers`, `shttp_servers`, and `stdio_servers` arrays, which OpenHands reads.
column4: Current OpenHands releases don't read MCP servers from a `config.toml` `[mcp]` section (`sse_servers`, `shttp_servers`, `stdio_servers`). That format belongs to legacy OpenHands (V0).

column3: `.windsurfignore` controls which files the agent may access, a different job from `.devinignore`, and only `.codeiumignore` is a legacy name.
column4: The legacy `.windsurfignore` and `.codeiumignore` filenames are still read and enforced alongside `.devinignore`. Existing files keep working, but prefer `.devinignore` for new rules.

column3: Antigravity names no frontmatter key for rules, so a bare Markdown file in `.agents/rules/` is an always-on rule.
column4: Every `.md` file inside `rules/` must start with YAML frontmatter declaring a valid `trigger`. If a file in `.agents/rules/*.md` omits frontmatter or specifies an unrecognized `trigger` value, Antigravity silently discards the rule.

column3: Hooks have no Kilo surface yet, so hook specs skip with a warning.
column4: Drop TypeScript or JavaScript files into a `plugin/` or `plugins/` folder inside any config directory: Project: `.kilo/plugin/`. Every `.ts` or `.js` file in those directories is auto-registered at startup. `tool.execute.before` fires before a tool runs.

column3: Hook handlers written to `.claude/settings.json` keep `timeout`, `statusMessage`, `if`, and `once`, and Claude Code honors each of them there.
column4: `once`: Only honored for hooks declared in skill frontmatter; ignored in settings files and agent frontmatter

column3: `taskOutputMaxChars` in `.claude/settings.json` sets the budget for background-task output, up to 128000.
column4: Removed the deprecated TaskOutput tool; Claude reads a background task's output file with Read instead, and the `taskOutputMaxChars` setting and `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` no longer have any effect

column3: Devin has no separate write tool, so `Write` and `Edit` both map to Devin's `edit` tool in `allowed-tools` and permission rules.
column4: Custom subagent profiles and skills can grant the `write` tool using `allowed-tools`, and permission rules recognize it.

column3: A stdio server in `.cursor/mcp.json` needs no `type` field, since Cursor infers stdio from `command`.
column4: For STDIO servers (local command-line servers), configure these fields in your `mcp.json`: type, Required: Yes, Server connection type, "stdio"

column3: Cursor discovers project skills only from `.cursor/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`.
column4: For compatibility, Cursor also loads skills from Claude and Codex directories: `.claude/skills/`, `.codex/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/`, and `~/.codex/skills/`.

column3: A project syncing `claude` and `amp` has every skill loaded twice by Amp, and whether Amp dedupes across the two roots is undocumented.
column4: Amp uses the first skill with a given frontmatter name. The order is: ~/.config/agents/skills/, ~/.agents/skills/, ~/.config/amp/skills/, .agents/skills/ in the project and searched parent directories, .claude/skills/ in those directories

column3: OpenCode has no hook surface, so hook specs skip with a warning.
column4: Plugins allow you to extend OpenCode by hooking into various events and customizing behavior. `.opencode/plugins/` - Project-level plugins. Files in these directories are automatically loaded at startup.

column3: An Antigravity rule scoped to files takes `trigger: glob` frontmatter with a comma-separated `globs` string.
column4: trigger: model_decision # Required: always_on, model_decision, glob, manual. globs: "*.ts, *.tsx" # Required for glob. `globs` is "Comma-separated file glob patterns".

column3: The OpenHands CLI reads MCP servers from `~/.openhands/mcp.json`.
column4: You can also manually edit the MCP configuration file at `~/.openhands/mcp.json`.

column3: Warp reads project MCP servers from `.warp/.mcp.json`.
column4: Warp reads MCP server definitions from the following providers: Warp, `.warp/.mcp.json` at project root. Project-scoped servers from any provider require explicit approval.

column3: An Antigravity Markdown agent can list hook files in its front matter.
column4: A Markdown agent can list hook files in its front matter with a hooks: entry.

column3: Cursor reads project MCP servers from `.cursor/mcp.json`.
column4: Each rule is truncated at 30,000 characters when included in a review. The combined rules Bugbot includes for a review are capped at 100,000 characters.

column3: Windsurf reads workspace rules from `.windsurf/rules/`.
column4: Direct file edits via the `edit` and `write` tools still prompt. These tools run inside the CLI process rather than inside the sandbox, so they cannot be bounded by it.

column3: Warp reads project rules from `AGENTS.md` at the repository root.
column4: Project-scoped servers from any provider require explicit approval.

column3: Antigravity reads project skills from `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
column4: `always_on` injects the full content into the system prompt on every turn. `manual` rules load only on an @-mention.

column3: `bashOutputMaxChars` in `.claude/settings.json` caps the Bash tool's output.
column4: Removed the deprecated TaskOutput tool; Claude reads a background task's output file with Read instead

column3: Augment reads hooks, MCP servers, and tool permissions only from a project's `.augment/settings.json`, and no user-tier settings file exists for Augment.
column4: `~/.augment/settings.json` | All | CLI, VSCode, IntelliJ | User-level settings (lowest precedence)

column3: Factory's agent file has no read-only mode, so a portable `readonly: true` agent field has no effect on Factory.
column4: `read-only` | `Read`, `LS`, `Grep`, `Glob` | Analysis and file exploration

column3: OpenHands's shttp MCP server entries in config.toml accept only `url`, `api_key`, and `timeout`, with no way to configure OAuth for a remote MCP server.
column4: Some MCP servers (like Notion MCP) require OAuth authentication instead of API keys. OpenHands supports OAuth-based MCP servers through the FastMCP library.

column3: Antigravity has no verified native directory-scoped or file-scoped instructions, so agnostic-ai skips a rule scoped to a subdirectory and writes nothing for it.
column4: Whenever Antigravity reads or edits a file, it walks up the directory tree from that file's folder to the workspace root, loading rules at each level:

column3: Cursor loads subagents only from `.cursor/agents/<name>.md`, and it does not cross-read `.claude/agents/` or `.codex/agents/` for Claude or Codex compatibility.
column4: When multiple locations contain subagents with the same name, `.cursor/` takes precedence over `.claude/` or `.codex/`.

column3: `AgentSpawn` is a valid Kiro CLI 3.0 hook trigger name, so agnostic-ai's validate accepts it for kiro hook specs.
column4: `agentSpawn` | `SessionStart` | Fires when a new session begins

column3: OpenCode's permission vocabulary has no key for MCP tools, so every portable mcp__ permission rule has nowhere to go on the opencode target.
column4: MCP server tools are registered with server name as prefix, so to disable all tools for a server simply use: `"mymcpservername_*": false`

column3: agnostic-ai writes Kiro CLI 3.0 hooks as standalone .kiro/hooks/<name>.json files with a versioned schema, which Kiro CLI 3.0 reads.
column4: Hooks have moved from embedded fields in agent config to standalone `.kiro/hooks/*.json` files with a versioned JSON schema.

column3: agnostic-ai writes a Gemini project's MCP servers and hooks to .gemini/settings.json at the project root, which Gemini CLI reads only when run from that project.
column4: Location: .gemini/settings.json within your project's root directory. Scope: Applies only when running Gemini CLI from that specific project.

column3: A Claude settings spec carrying x-claude: {disabledMcpjsonServers: [name]} reaches the project-tier rejection list Claude Code reads for .mcp.json servers.
column4: A rejection in any settings file applies, including a project `.claude/settings.json` checked into the repository.

column3: OpenHands's config.toml [mcp] table reads stdio_servers entries with a command and args list, the same shape as sse_servers.
column4: fix(mcp): keep OAuth credentials on cloud saves and skip consent when tokens still work

column3: Antigravity's default project entry-point file, .agent/AGENTS.md, accepts YAML frontmatter to scope which files it applies to.
column4: All active global and always_on rules share a 20,000-token budget separate from the customization budget (plugins such as skills and MCP).

column3: Every entry in a Kiro CLI 3.0 .kiro/hooks/*.json file requires a matcher field, even for triggers that fire once per session.
column4: `Manual` | User-triggered on demand

column3: Droid CLI evaluates every shell command against commandAllowlist, commandDenylist, and commandBlocklist, the current command policy keys in .factory/settings.json.
column4: `commandAllowlist`, `commandDenylist`, and `commandBlocklist` are deprecated, not removed. Existing lists remain respected for backward compatibility. Use permission rules for new policy.

column3: A camelCase Copilot hook event tests its matcher as a plain regex against Copilot's own lowercase tool names.
column4: Supports an optional `matcher` field that filters by agent name. The value is treated as a regular expression wrapped as `^(?:matcher)$` and tested against `agentName`.

column3: taskOutputMaxChars is still emitted because it works on the older stable release.
column4: `taskOutputMaxChars` | Removed in v2.1.277, together with the `TaskOutput` tool it sized

column3: Since v2.1.277, a session with no CLAUDE.md at or above the working directory loads AGENTS.md.
column4: Before v2.1.281, some sessions, such as those on Amazon Bedrock or with telemetry disabled, read `CLAUDE.md` files only.

column3: Per-agent `mcpServers` has no agnostic-ai field, so set it through `x-gemini`; Gemini reads it from the agent frontmatter.
column4: mcp_servers: z.record(mcpServerSchema).optional(), model: z.string().optional(), temperature: z.number().optional(), max_turns: z.number().int().positive().optional(), timeout_mins: z.number().int().positive().optional(), }) .strict();

column3: copilot reads its MCP file from `.vscode/mcp.json` in the project, where agnostic-ai writes it by default.
column4: Choose .mcp.json to save a portable configuration at the workspace root. The flow also lists the deprecated .vscode/mcp.json and VS Code user-profile destinations for compatibility. Prefer the portable destinations for new servers.

column3: Kiro CLI V3 applies `.kiroignore` only to content and filename search results.
column4: In CLI V3, a workspace `.kiroignore` blocks matching files from direct reads and filters them from content and filename search results.

column3: Kiro CLI V3 hooks accept eleven triggers: SessionStart, Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreTaskExec, PostTaskExec, UserPromptSubmit, PostFileCreate, PostFileSave, PostFileDelete, and Manual; validate rejects any other trigger for kiro.
column4: Use the new `SessionEnd` trigger to run a Hook when a V3 session shuts down.

column3: Explicit alwaysLoad:false can be omitted because it has the default loading meaning.
column4: Changed MCP server `alwaysLoad: false` to defer all of that server's tools behind tool search

column3: Claude project MCP entries need only the existing transport, timeout, alwaysLoad and oauth fields for handshake compatibility.
column4: add "bareElicitationCapability": true to its MCP config entry

column3: A Kiro custom agent loads only the files its resources list names.
column4: By default, custom agents inherit default resources (steering files, skills, and AGENTS.md) alongside their own configured resources.

column3: Kiro steering inclusion modes other than always and fileMatch carry no meaning for import.
column4: Kiro CLI V3 supports all four inclusion modes: `always`, `fileMatch`, `manual`, and `auto`.
